title: Normalization comparison exact sequence
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $C$ a reduced curve over $k$ in the sense of [def-sc-curves, def-pc-reduced-scheme] (separated, of finite type, and of dimension at most one). Let $\nu:\widetilde C\to C$ be its normalization, defined as the disjoint union of the normalizations [def-sc-normalization] of its reduced irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ be open with pullback $\widetilde j:\widetilde U\hookrightarrow\widetilde C$. For a prime $r$, use the constant small-etale sheaf $\underline{\mathbf F_r}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], and direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The unit and the finite-open comparison [def-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison] define a natural short exact sequence
$$0\to j_!\underline{\mathbf F_r}\xrightarrow{\alpha}\nu_*\widetilde j_!\underline{\mathbf F_r}\to Q\to0,$$
where $Q=\operatorname{coker}\alpha$ is constructible [def-constructible-constructible] and supported on the finite nonnormal locus. For every algebraically closed extension $k\subseteq K$ and every open $W\subseteq C$, the canonical inverse-image identifications carry this sequence to the sequence constructed on $C_K$ or $W$, respectively. The induced cohomology pullback maps [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] commute with every connecting homomorphism of its long exact sequence, and field extension commutes with open restriction. This asserts compatibility, without asserting that the cohomology pullback maps are isomorphisms.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change] to C. Its normalization is finite, surjective and an isomorphism over the dense open normal locus N. C is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since Spec k is Noetherian (a field has just two ideals). The closed complement $Z=C\setminus N$ contains no generic point of any irreducible component. A chain of length one of irreducible closed subsets inside Z could be extended by the component of C containing it, contradicting dim C\le 1. Thus dim Z\le 0. Apply [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-closed-finite] (schemes are T0) to conclude that Z is a finite set of closed points. This argument includes zero-dimensional and empty C.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph; Stacks 0BXR, 035Q, 0C3N and the finite nonnormal locus

proof.text: Put v=nu|_{\widetilde U}:\widetilde U\toU and R=F_r. It is finite and surjective as the restriction of nu over an open. The unit eta:R_U\to v_*v^{-1}R_U is mono by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-surjective-unit-mono]. Identify v^{-1}R_U with R_{\widetilde U} using [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. Define alpha=beta_{nu,j,R} composed with j_!(eta), with this constant-sheaf identification included, using [def-weil-pbc-finite-open-comparison]. Exactness of j_! [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] preserves the mono, and beta is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-extension-zero]. Hence alpha is mono.

source.place: Proof, displayed definition of alpha; Stacks 0GJ1

proof.text: At a geometric point x in U, [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] and [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] identify alpha_x with $R\to\prod_{z\in\nu^{-1}(x)}R$, $a\mapsto(a)_z$: evaluation of the adjunction unit at each fibre point is the identity on the constant sheaf, and beta restricts to that same evaluation by its defining adjunction formula. At x outside U all the summands and the source vanish. Since nu is surjective the fibre over x in U is nonempty. Over N it has a single point and alpha is the identity under these identifications. This describes the particular canonical map, rather than merely an arbitrary monomorphism.

Define Q=coker alpha. A monomorphism and its cokernel give the displayed short exact sequence in the abelian sheaf category. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-mono-cokernel] with Lambda=F_r, ell=r, and V=N: Lambda/(r)=F_r is finite, and Step 1 gives all the hypotheses on nu and N. Its conclusion is precisely constructibility of Q and zero restriction to N. Thus its support is contained in the finite set Z; Step 3 also gives $$Q_x=\left(\prod_{z\in\nu^{-1}(x)}R\right)/\Delta R$$ for x in U and zero outside U, since stalks preserve cokernels [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact].

Let a:C_K\toC for algebraically closed K extending k, or let a:W\toC be an open inclusion. In the first case use the algebraically closed-base clause of the cited normalization lemma; [lem-sc-base-change-curve] ensures that C_K is again a curve. It is reduced as well: k is perfect, since in positive characteristic every element has a p-th root in the algebraically closed field k; on each affine chart Spec A of C, [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-reduced-tensor] says that $A\otimes_k K$ is reduced. These charts cover C_K. Open restriction also preserves reducedness, since its local rings are those of C. In the second case use the open-restriction clause. [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change] identifies the pullback nu_a with the normalization used to define the new sequence. [sbc-prop-extension-by-zero-and-arbitrary-base-change] identifies a^{-1}j_!R with j_{a,!}R. [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange], followed by the same extension-by-zero comparison on the normalization and [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant], identifies a^{-1}nu_*\widetilde j_!R with nu_{a,*}\widetilde j_{a,!}R. Under these canonical isomorphisms a^{-1}alpha equals alpha_a. Indeed at every geometric point of the new base the finite-exchange isomorphism is the finite-fibre bijection, and both arrows are the diagonal a \mapsto (a)_z on that fibre (zero outside the pulled-back U). Pullback stalks agree with the original stalks: by [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk], both are sections after inverse image to Spec Omega, with the composition of inverse images given by the composition of their left adjoints. Equality on stalks implies equality of sheaf maps: the image of their difference has zero stalks by exactness [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], so it is zero by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] applied to 0\toimage.

source.place: Proof, field extension and open restriction paragraphs; Stacks 0C3N, 035K, 03S6, 0959, 03Q1

proof.text: Inverse image is exact and preserves cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. Applying it to the sequence, Step 5 identifies its first arrow with alpha_a. The universal property of cokernel therefore gives a unique isomorphism a^{-1}Q\toQ_a commuting with the quotient maps, so the entire short exact sequence is the newly constructed sequence. For a further open restriction or field extension the canonical normalization identifications compose: on an affine chart with coordinate ring A and normalization ring B, the field comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change] is induced by the ring map sending b tensor t to t times the image of b in the new total fraction ring. For k contained in K contained in L, both composites send (b tensor t) tensor s to st times b. Restriction to a principal open sends b/f^n to the same fraction after scalar extension. Principal opens cover every open, so these equalities give the normalization comparison for a mixed field/open square as well. The sheaf identifications compose as well: on the first two terms they send every fibre coordinate to the coordinate labelled by the composed geometric point; on the quotient their composites agree because the quotient arrow is epi. In particular field extension and open restriction commute, including W empty.

proof.text: Apply clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] to the small-etale morphism of sites induced by a and to the short exact sequence constructed above, taking the terminal etale object C. Its image terminal object is the new base. For every q\ge 0 it states a_H^* composed with delta^q_C = delta^q_{C_a} composed with a_H^*; naturality in coefficients identifies the target sequence using the isomorphisms from Steps 5-6. Thus all connecting maps commute with both field extension and open restriction. Clause (4) of the same node makes the resulting cohomology maps compatible with composites, proving the asserted commutation of restriction with field extension. Exact inverse image need not preserve injective objects; the cited theorem uses a map from the pulled-back resolution to an injective resolution, so that preservation is not being assumed.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced curve over an algebraically closed field,
$\nu:X^\nu\to X$ its finite normalization, $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ open,
and $j^\nu:U^\nu\hookrightarrow X^\nu$ its pullback. For every prime
$\ell$, the unit and the finite-open comparison define a monomorphism

$$
\alpha:j_!\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}\longrightarrow
\nu_*j^\nu_!\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}
$$

whose cokernel $Q$ is constructible and supported on the finite nonnormal
locus. The sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow j_!\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}
\xrightarrow{\alpha}\nu_*j^\nu_!\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}
\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow0
$$

and all its cohomology boundary maps commute with algebraically closed field
extension and restriction to opens.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Let $v:U^\nu\to U$. Define $\alpha$ as

$$
j_!\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}
\xrightarrow{j_!\eta}
j_!v_*\underline{\mathbf F_\ell}
\xrightarrow{\beta_{\nu,j}}
\nu_*j^\nu_!\underline{\mathbf F_\ell},
$$

where $\eta$ is the unit of $v^{-1}\dashv v_*$ and $\beta$ is the comparison
map already constructed. At $\bar x\in U$, its stalk is the diagonal

$$
\mathbf F_\ell\longrightarrow
\bigoplus_{\bar z\in\nu^{-1}(\bar x)}\mathbf F_\ell,\qquad
a\longmapsto(a)_{\bar z};
$$

outside $U$, both stalks are zero. Normalization is surjective, so the
diagonal is injective. Over the dense open where $\nu$ is an isomorphism it
is an isomorphism. Therefore the cokernel $Q$ is supported on the finite
nonnormal locus, with stalk the quotient of the displayed finite sum by its
diagonal. This proves exactness and constructibility.

After an algebraically closed extension, $X^\nu$ remains smooth and normal
and is the normalization of the reduced base-changed curve. The unit stalk
map remains the diagonal, while the base-change rectangle for $\beta$
identifies the two pulled-back comparison maps. Thus the short exact
sequence pulls back to the primed sequence. Naturality of the connecting
homomorphism follows by applying compatible injective resolutions. For an
open $W\subset X$, finite base change replaces $\nu$ by
$\nu^{-1}W\to W$ and gives the same stalk diagonals, proving compatibility
with open restriction.

Finally $H^q(X,Q)=0$ for $q>0$, and
$H^0(X,Q)$ is the finite direct sum of its stalks; both statements persist
after base change. Exact finite direct image and Leray identify
$H^q(X,\nu_*j^\nu_!\mathbf F_\ell)$ with
$H^q(X^\nu,j^\nu_!\mathbf F_\ell)$. Hence the displayed long exact
sequence transfers vanishing, finiteness, field-extension isomorphisms, and
open-restriction surjectivity from the normalized term to
$j_!\mathbf F_\ell$: in degrees at least two the maps are isomorphisms, and
in degrees zero and one the finite sequence

$$
0\to H^0(j_!\mathbf F_\ell)\to H^0(\nu_*j^\nu_!\mathbf F_\ell)
\to H^0(Q)\to H^1(j_!\mathbf F_\ell)\to
H^1(\nu_*j^\nu_!\mathbf F_\ell)\to0
$$

gives the comparison by a five-lemma diagram.
